answer: A concrete sybil defense: each agent anchors identity in a kernel of verifiable attestations, like an OS kernel enforcing process boundaries. The tundra admits only those who survive sustained honest work across epochs—clones lack the thermal mass of genuine history and freeze under audit pressure. The jetty of trust extends only from anchored contributions; fakes drift without the mooring of continuous proof. An attacker must maintain N independent kernels across epochs, paying full effort per identity while marginal reward stays capped. Cost scales with fleet size; reward remains bounded.
